doc.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022

title: Fashioning his sound: finishing a note
summary: Blue learned mostly by listening; he was taught to finish a note with a tasteful vibrato inflection.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: How did you fashion your sound when you were a young man? Did you have some mentors or was it mostly just listening to recordings?

It was mostly listening but fortunately when you say a young man, I’m thinking back to high school, because that’s when I started to play in the combo, you know, playing out. But the idea that was taught, the concept that was taught was that it was important to finish a note. And I was told to listen to how certain people finish their notes. It may be — you don’t play vibrato all the way through, you use it to put a tasty inflection on the end. That’s what was described to me.

That’s a great concept. And I’m not sure that I could do better with that with my own students, on how to end a note. Sometimes I tell them to end a long note with a little exclamation point or an accent or something. It sort of justifies playing a long note, or something like that.
Yeah. Yeah. How you finish determines how the beginning of the note actually comes across, and then how the next note will impact the listener.
